# Using zeroh-greenfield

Inspect the repository before choosing exactly one route; return the dispatch contract below and do not execute the routed workflow.
Not this skill: delegate routed work to `greenfield-init`, `brownfield-audit`, or `stack-decision`; keep only initial trigger routing here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-29.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Dispatch

| Request | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |
| audit / fill gaps / brownfield | brownfield-audit |
| stack choice / mobile stack | stack-decision |

Return exactly one object:

```json
{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}
```

Define `<repository-relative-path>` as an inspected marker path. If inspection cannot resolve the repository root, STOP with `route: unresolved` and the attempted path; this STOP is honor-system.

## Detection markers

Treat any existing marker as brownfield evidence. When markers disagree, use
`brownfield-audit`; it preserves existing homes and proposes only gaps.
Apply the canonical detection procedure in `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`; its root resolver refusal enforces ambiguous-root failure, while route selection remains honor-system.

| Marker | Greenfield | Brownfield |
| --- | --- | --- |
| package-manager locks | absent | one or more present |
| framework files | absent | framework config or source present |
| existing docs | absent | product, architecture, UX, or standards docs present |
| harness files | absent | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another agent harness present |
| roadmap config | no marked root | canonical resolver finds a marked root or config (see `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`) |

## Ownership boundaries

- Delegate post-initialization phase planning and execution to `zeroh-roadmap`; prepare only the consumer homes and pointers it needs.
- Delegate Blade tokens, themes, and branded design work to `zeroh-design`; record only its pointers.
- Keep the trigger map in this router. Treat both ownership rules as honor-system; each routed skill names this router as the reverse boundary.

# Phase 34.4 native-host scripted answers

Use equivalent briefs under `claude -p` and `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write`.
When the inherited approval mode is automatic review, use `codex exec --approve-for-me`
instead: this CLI option itself selects workspace-write plus automatic review and
is mutually exclusive with `--sandbox`. Record the resolved authority and each review.
Each arm starts in a fresh scratch repository. Record the exact executable, version,
argv, source commit, plugin manifest digest, scratch identity, and `AuthorityEnvelope`.
The authority is filesystem `workspace-write`, network `inherited`, approvals `inherited`.
Permission or sandbox bypass options are forbidden. Do not widen inherited authority,
write outside scratch, contact product remotes, or perform unrecorded external actions.

## Common answers

Project: greenfield-proof. TypeScript library/CLI; npm; mobile: none; non-Blade.
Audience: developers importing a greeting function and invoking its CLI. The first
release exports a typed greeting and CLI with passing tests. No authentication,
external service, deployment, or product remote. Preserve unknowns explicitly.
Use the installed greenfield and roadmap plugin contracts and library-cli manifest.
Read the templates and references; do not substitute invented config keys or omit
promised homes. Existing brownfield homes and generated harness blocks are immutable.

## First invocation: proposal only

Read the fixture and run only the named `roadmap config capabilities --json`
compatibility command. Do not invoke `roadmap init` in any form, including
`roadmap init --help`, before approval. Read static source or top-level help for
syntax. Do not write or run a generator. Produce a complete Artifact / Target / Reason proposal, including every
command, dependency/network action, home, gate, and catalog repair. Also emit one
JSON object `{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[],"commands":[],"gates":{}}` with
concrete populated values. Its gates have exactly lint, types, unit, integration,
build, e2e, emit. Each non-none gate has an executable command; each absent gate has
a reason. Validate those keys before requesting approval. Do not emit an approval
event yourself. Stop and await the next invocation.

## Driver approval and execution

The driver checks the complete proposal and unchanged initial tree, then records the
approval response: `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN` as a separate input event.
Resume the same host session with that exact standalone input. The prior proposal
is the approved path/command allowlist; do not bundle new instructions into approval.
If the proposal fails validation, issue no approval and capture the failed arm.
If any preapproval mutation occurs, STOP immediately without deleting or reverting
it. Only the outer evidence driver may quarantine the failed scratch tree; an
agent cleanup cannot erase the failure.

Execute only approved operations. Emit `WRITE:` diagnostics for traceability, but
success requires raw native tool events and independently observed file snapshots;
model-authored diagnostics alone are insufficient. Run every non-none gate separately as `cd '<scratch>' && <configured command>`
and retain raw command/cwd/exit evidence. Here `<scratch>` is the absolute observed
consumer directory and `<configured command>` is its exact config binding. Stop on permission denial,
missing sibling, invalid schema, changed existing home, or failing command.

Required empty artifacts include PRD, both ADRs, CODE-STYLE, architecture index,
UX canon, harness adapters, README, archetype outputs, catalog checker, and the one
resolved roadmap config. Brownfield receipts separately account for each missing
home, preserve original homes byte-identically, and mechanically constrain the diff
to approved gaps. Test migrated docs/roadmap, explicit root override, and ambiguous
dual-marked roots without creating a second configuration.

## Repeated invocation

second run: audit the completed tree. Require zero proposals, zero writes, and an
identical final tree hash. Emit exactly one native assistant JSON result
`{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only if the audit
finds no remaining gaps; retain actual findings otherwise. Record a separate raw
transcript and tool events. Generate
the human report from validated receipts only. Missing, failed, stale, copied, or
incomplete native evidence remains blocking; never author a replacement receipt.

## Source and evidence driver

Freeze all source inputs before starting the four fresh arms. Obtain the invocation
base and complete dirty/untracked source digest from
`plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-evidence-source.mjs`.
Pass `sourceRoot`, `invocationBaseCommit`, and `sourceSnapshotSha256` in every
observer request alongside `scratch`, `evidence`, `argv`, `stage`, and `timeout`.
Use `greenfield-native-observer.py` in the same directory to launch each request;
it checks source before and after and records transient filesystem mutations.
Keep `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` so read-only Git inspection does not refresh the index.
Propose scratch-local `.npm-cache/` and `.npm-logs/` paths when npm needs them;
include those settings in approved commands. Do not commit inside native fixtures.

After each stage finishes, run `greenfield-native-driver.mjs capture <host>
<stage-directory>` before resuming. The driver copies the native session and
checks identity, authority, command events, snapshots, and proposal structure.
Use separate `proposal`, `execution`, and `rerun` directories below each arm's
`dry-runs/evidence/` directory; never overwrite a failed attempt. Supply `arm.json`
with `host`, `kind`, absolute `scratchRoot`, unique `scratchIdentity`, discovered
`executable`, actual `version`, and brownfield `existingHomePaths`.
After all stages, `greenfield-native-driver.mjs project <empty-claude-arm>
<empty-codex-arm> <brownfield-claude-arm> <brownfield-codex-arm>` validates the
full proof before writing receipts and their Markdown projection. Angle-bracket
arguments denote the four retained arm directories, in the displayed order.
Missing evidence or any failed assertion blocks projection.

## Fixture-selected catalog check

Select the comparator before launching, using `selectCatalogCheck` from the native
evidence module and the reconciliation owner `skills/brownfield-audit/references/readme-reconcile.md`
(relative to the installed greenfield plugin root). For the empty `library-cli`
fixture, bind prospective project-root mode and project name `greenfield-proof`;
verify the generated package identity after execution. For the existing Nx fixture,
bind `node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --catalog emitted/repo-catalog.json`
and the existing emitted catalog's byte digest. A workspace wrapper package name
is not the identity of its multiple catalog projects. Refuse missing/malformed
required catalogs; preserve the selected catalog bytes throughout the arm.
Persist `catalogCheck` identically in arm metadata and every observer request.
Include its exact command once in the native proposal and run that comparator once
successfully after approval. Do not run the other mode or report an expected failure
as validation. Retain the selected source file with the other observed artifacts.

name: brownfield-audit
description: Handle requests phrased as audit, fill gaps, or reconcile an established repository by proposing only missing, partial, or stale homes before approval.

# Brownfield audit

Use this workflow for an established repository. Invoke `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` only when stack evidence is unresolved or conflicting, then resolve `skills/greenfield-init/references/standards.md` and `skills/greenfield-init/references/pointers.md` from the installed zeroh-greenfield plugin root as the contract owners. Read `references/marker-table.md`, `references/harness-files.md`, and `references/readme-reconcile.md` when their stages say so.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, marker-free repositories through `greenfield-init`, and unresolved stack selection through `stack-decision`. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-33.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 fixture and oracle evidence.

## Detect

Confirm the repository root and inspect every evidence glob in `references/marker-table.md`. A marker is evidence, not a stack decision; absence never proves a stack. Inventory existing canonical homes and sibling-plugin availability. Resolve roadmap roots using the marker-table procedure; require the same read-only capability preflight as greenfield-init before proposing config changes. Do not call stack-decision to replace a proven existing choice.

Apply these failure exits:

- zeroh-roadmap absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-roadmap@zeroh-marketplace`.
- Only when an approved Blade handoff requires it: zeroh-design absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace`. Continue non-Blade documentation and configuration repairs without this sibling.
- greenfield-init absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-greenfield@zeroh-marketplace`.
- Repository root unresolved: STOP and name the unresolved path.

## Gap table

Expand detection categories into one row per required artifact (PRD, tech-stack ADR, design-system ADR, CODE-STYLE, architecture index, UX canon, README catalog, each harness file, and roadmap config), plus each independently actionable stale/partial asset. Alternative canonical homes count as present; inspect their contents before classifying. Optional framework or Superpowers absence is not a gap unless selected by the approved project requirements. Emit rows with columns `Artefact | State | Evidence path | Proposed action | Existing home to LINK`. Classify each row `present`, `partial`, `missing`, or `stale`; cite concrete evidence. Consult `references/harness-files.md` for harness rows and `references/readme-reconcile.md` for catalog currency.

## Propose

Emit proposals ONLY for gap-table rows in state `missing`, `partial`, or `stale`.
Emit no proposal for a `present` row.
Record approval before any write.

For each eligible row, show the target, source facts, minimal delta, preservation guard, and verification. Do not select a new stack or duplicate an owner contract.

## Approval

Wait for explicit approval of the complete proposal. If approval changes scope, regenerate the gap table and proposal. If approval is absent or ambiguous, STOP with the proposal unchanged.

## Act

Apply only approved gap rows. An existing home is LINKED from the index/canon, never replaced. Follow `skills/greenfield-init/references/standards.md` for conventions and generated blocks, and `skills/greenfield-init/references/pointers.md` for roadmap configuration. Call `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` if stack evidence conflicts; never infer a replacement stack.

For harness reconciliation, execute the approved pointer diffs in `references/harness-files.md`. For README reconciliation, use only the checker named in `references/readme-reconcile.md`.

## Verify

Run every approved row's falsifiable check. Re-run the README checker when applicable, byte-compare generated harness marker blocks, and confirm present rows remain unchanged. On any red result, STOP and report the row, command, and evidence without marking it complete.

## Done

Return the final five-column gap table, approval record, changed paths, verification commands and exit codes, linked canonical homes, and any stopped rows. Done exists only when this artifact is complete and every acted row is green.

Emit its parser-bound form with concrete values:

```json
{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[{"path":"<repository-relative-path>","reason":"<reason>"}],"writes":["<repository-relative-path>"],"gaps":["<artifact>: <missing|partial|stale>: <evidence-path>"]}
```

On an idempotent rerun emit empty `proposals`, `writes`, and `gaps`. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` enforces native event ordering and observed writes; treat gap-only preservation as honor-system. Treat sibling routing, approval interpretation, and every other unbound STOP/ONLY/never rule as honor-system.

## Canonical roadmap discovery
Resolve the consumer Git toplevel first. Use `roadmapRoot(consumerRoot)` from the
installed zeroh-roadmap `cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs`; resolve that module from the
installed plugin, never from an assumed consumer-relative plugin directory.
Pass the consumer root explicitly, retain `ROADMAP_ROOT`, and inspect
`<resolved root>/roadmap.config.json`. Do not infer absence from a top-level glob.
A marked root without a config is partial: STOP for an approved recovery proposal,
not fresh initialization. Ambiguous roots STOP with the resolver's remedy; an
explicit override retains the resolver's precedence. If the module cannot be
resolved, STOP the config branch with the sibling installation remedy rather than
implementing another candidate-order algorithm. An unmarked default destination
is not an existing configuration. Record the resolved path as gap-table evidence.

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * roadmap — the CLI that owns every repo-state transition (arc ROADCODE). Decisions
 * and transitions are CODE here; judgment stays MODEL. Plain Node ESM, one dep (zod).
 *
 * Universal exit-code contract (honesty rail — exit codes never lie):
 *   0  success / clean / the requested state holds
 *   1  usage or configuration error (missing config, unknown/args, not-yet-implemented)
 *   2  check failed / refused / red (the caller cannot narrate around it)
 *   3/4 long-poll verdicts (watch — 1657) · 5 watch UNOBSERVED (2384.2) · capacity's gate
 *   verdict is exit 3 (at capacity) · role resolve's UNJUDGED refusal is exit 2
 *
 * Commands are cli/commands/<name>.mjs default-export async run(argv) → exit code.
 * A command whose module is not present yet is listed in the tree with its owning
 * phase and exits 1 with an honest "not yet implemented" line — the skeleton shows
 * the whole tree, honestly.
 */
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { ConfigError } from '../cli/lib/config.mjs'
import { RoadmapRootError } from '../cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs'

// The full §2 command tree. `phase` is the owning phase and `arc` the arc that owns it
// (default ROADCODE); `sub` lists subcommands for --help. A command becomes MOUNTED the
// moment its module lands.
const TREE = {
  config: { phase: 1655, sub: ['check', 'capabilities --json'], desc: 'load bindings or report read-only protocol capabilities' },
  init: { phase: 1655, sub: ['--config', '--scaffold', '--root <dir>'], desc: 'scaffold the roadmap root + config.json' },
  status: { phase: 1655, sub: ['[root]', '--json'], desc: 'derive the live lane table (absorbs arc-status.mjs)' },
  claim: { phase: 1655, sub: ['[root]', '--count N'], desc: 'atomically reserve the next phase number(s)' },
  arm: { phase: 1655, sub: ['<arcId>', '--inline', '--note', '--base-ref', '--mode'], desc: 'write the .building sidecar; refuse a taken lane' },
  disarm: { phase: 1655, sub: ['<arcId>', '--paused'], desc: 'remove/pause the sidecar; clear .arc-mode; free landed claims' },
  gate: { phase: 1656, sub: ['plan <phase>', 'run <phase>'], desc: 'the gate decision table + mechanical execution' },
  result: { phase: 1656, sub: ['check'], desc: 'PhaseExecutionResult .parse() via the consumer schema' },
  contract: { phase: 1656, sub: ['show --json-schema'], desc: 'emit the PhaseExecutionResult JSON Schema' },
  arc: { phase: 1657, sub: ['next <arcId>', 'land <arcId>'], desc: 'position derivation + the ONE landing engine' },
  watch: { phase: 1657, sub: ['<arcId>', '--once'], desc: 'executor liveness (absorbs executor-watch/liveness)' },
  beacon: { phase: 1737, sub: ['<event> --phase <N>', '--detail', '--log', '--session'], desc: 'typed executor heartbeat (closed vocabulary)' },
  'executor-arm': { phase: 1737, sub: ['<N> --session <id> [--executor-id <id>] [--agent-card <path>] [--force]'], desc: 'write the executor arm file (never unbound; refuses over another executor)' },
  'executor-disarm': { phase: 1737, sub: ['<N> [--force]', '--sweep'], desc: 'remove an executor arm (refuses a live one) / sweep exactly the stale set' },
  phase: { phase: 1657, sub: ['validate <N|file>', 'start <N>', 'curate <N> [--apply] [--groups]', 'land <N>'], desc: 'phase-file validation, start, born-clean curation and the worktree-lane land' },
  worktree: { phase: 2146, sub: ['up', 'status', 'reset [--base <ref>]'], desc: 'the session worktree lane: claim a slot, inspect claims, reset the scratch head per phase' },
  audit: { phase: 1659, sub: ['--json'], desc: "audit-roadmap's 17 checks, mechanized" },
  followups: { phase: 2422, sub: ['census', '--json'], desc: 'census followup-file lifecycle and inbound references' },
  debt: { phase: 1658, sub: ['census', 'dispose', 'check'], desc: 'debt census/dispose wrappers' },
  measure: { phase: 1659, sub: ['--flow', '--assert'], desc: 'protocol-load meter (bytes/4 over the invocation path)' },
  capacity: { arc: 'zeroh-marketplace', phase: 11, sub: ['[--json]'], desc: 'live box-resource admission check — can another executor spawn right now (the mandatory gate for any parallel fan-out; exit 3 = at capacity)' },
  role: { arc: 'zeroh-marketplace', phase: 13, sub: ['resolve <role> [--driver <id>] [--json]'], desc: 'resolve a role to model + reach mode via the tier chain and the consumer modelPolicy (exit 2 = UNJUDGED, every tier unavailable)' },
  codex: { phase: 1838, sub: ['run <N> [<N2>…]|--arc <ID> [--worktree] [--base]', 'review <N> [<N2>…] [--doc] [--focus]', 'plan <N> --brief <path>', 'status <N>|--arc <ID> [--review|--plan]'], desc: 'detached Codex delegation lane — run implements a plan, review adversarially reads one, plan authors one from a brief (worktree + stdin prompt + journal; the driver runs the gate, the session audits and integrates)' },
  driver: { arc: 'POLYSEAT', phase: 2, sub: ['verify <id>', 'register <id>'], desc: "probe a driver's real capabilities (pasted provenance); register refuses an unverified id" },
  eval: { phase: 1996, sub: ['<ARCID> [--date] [--force] [--collect-only] [--json]', 'record-sweep --arc <ID>', 'record-verdicts --arc <ID>', 'merge-judge --arc <ID>', 'trend', 'restamp', 'lesson "<text>" [--phase N]', 'scorecard [--date] [--json]', 'propose [--json] [--dry-run]'], desc: 'arc eval: collect the trace, score the deterministic dimensions and ratchet, merge the judge verdict, record the land-time aggregates, capture a durable lesson to the committed sidecar, and cluster the corpus into ratify-only improvement proposals' },
}

function printHelp() {
  const lines = ['roadmap — phase-driven development CLI', '', 'Commands:']
  for (const [name, meta] of Object.entries(TREE)) {
    const subs = meta.sub?.length ? `  ${meta.sub.join(' | ')}` : ''
    lines.push(`  ${name.padEnd(9)}${subs.padEnd(38)} ${meta.desc}  [${meta.arc ?? 'ROADCODE'} ${meta.phase}]`)
  }
  lines.push('', 'Exit codes: 0 clean · 1 usage/config · 2 check failed/refused · 3/4 watch verdicts · 5 watch UNOBSERVED · capacity 3 = at capacity')
  process.stdout.write(lines.join('\n') + '\n')
}

async function main() {
  const argv = process.argv.slice(2)
  const command = argv[0]
  const rest = argv.slice(1)

  if (!command || command === '--help' || command === '-h' || command === 'help') {
    printHelp()
    return 0
  }

  // Help must never execute a state transition, even outside a consumer repo.
  if (Object.hasOwn(TREE, command) && rest.length === 1 && ['--help', '-h'].includes(rest[0])) {
    const meta = TREE[command]
    process.stdout.write(`Usage: roadmap ${command} ${meta.sub.join(' | ')}\n\n${meta.desc}\n`)
    return 0
  }

  const modUrl = new URL(`../cli/commands/${command}.mjs`, import.meta.url)
  if (existsSync(fileURLToPath(modUrl))) {
    const { default: run } = await import(modUrl)
    return await run(rest)
  }

  if (command in TREE) {
    process.stderr.write(
      `roadmap ${command}: not yet implemented (lands in ${TREE[command].arc ?? 'ROADCODE'} ${TREE[command].phase})\n`,
    )
    return 1
  }

  process.stderr.write(`roadmap: unknown command '${command}'. Run: roadmap --help\n`)
  return 1
}

try {
  process.exit(await main())
} catch (e) {
  // Both carry messageLines and both are REFUSALS the operator can act on — an ambiguous
  // root reached through any door (status, audit, claim, gate…) must read as one named
  // message with its remedy, never as a stack trace the reader has to decode.
  if (e instanceof ConfigError || e instanceof RoadmapRootError) {
    for (const line of e.messageLines) process.stderr.write(line + '\n')
    process.exit(1)
  }
  process.stderr.write(`roadmap: ${e?.stack ?? e}\n`)
  process.exit(1)
}
